subject: Flight Performance and Planning
question_text: How does a headwind affect the still-air best-range speed, and what is the usual technique?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Range is increased, and speed should be reduced

choices.label: B
choices.text: Range is unchanged, because airspeed is unchanged

choices.label: C
choices.text: Range is reduced, and the speed should be reduced well below best-range speed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Range is reduced, and the best-range speed is increased slightly

explanation: A headwind lowers ground speed, so less ground is covered per litre. Flying a little faster than the still-air best-range speed shortens the time spent in the headwind and improves ground range.

incorrect_answer_explanations.A: A headwind reduces ground speed and so ground range.
incorrect_answer_explanations.B: Ground range depends on ground speed.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: Flying slower in a headwind leaves the aeroplane exposed to the wind for longer.
